evals.prompt: We have a vague idea: let hotel guests check in and unlock their room using their phone instead of a physical key card. Write a PR-FAQ for this before we commit any engineering resources.
evals.expected_output: Produces a press release (headline, sub-headline, summary, problem, solution, a company spokesperson quote, and a specific customer quote) plus a two-part FAQ covering both external/customer questions and internal/technical questions.

assertions.text: Includes a customer quote attributed to a named guest/customer, not just a spokesperson line
Includes distinct External and Internal FAQ sections, not just the phrase PR-FAQ

evals.prompt:
Review this draft PR-FAQ and tell me what's wrong with it before we bring it to the approval meeting:

---
HEADLINE: New Platform Capability Launched

Today we are launching a new capability on our platform that gives users more flexibility and control. This has been a top priority for the team and represents a significant investment in our infrastructure.

"We're thrilled to bring this new capability to our users," said a company spokesperson. "This is exactly what our customers have been asking for."

Get started today by visiting our website.
---
evals.expected_output: Flags that the headline is vague/generic, that there is no real customer quote (only a generic spokesperson line), and that the FAQ section is missing entirely, and recommends rewriting before approval rather than approving as-is.

assertions.text: Flags the missing or weak customer quote
Flags that the FAQ section is missing entirely from the draft

evals.prompt: We need to add a 'sort by price' dropdown to an existing internal admin table that already has sort-by-date and sort-by-name. Should we write a full PR-FAQ for this, or something else? Explain your recommendation.
evals.expected_output: Recommends a lighter one-page PRD instead of a full PR-FAQ, explaining that the feature is a well-understood extension with no real customer-value ambiguity, so a press release exercise would be unnecessary overhead.

assertions.text: Recommends against a full PR-FAQ for this case
Mentions PRD or a simpler alternative
